Messages.Author: Snoop
Messages.Body:
If you have two guns a .44 and a SNS for example... You take the maneuver of
the .44, then the opponent play canine horde with sup ANI... my 44 is down,
but can i shoot with the saturday Night Special instead? or am i forced to
use the .44 that i doesn't have anymore... so doing no strike ...? (BTW you
can dodge a canine horde, even with first strike ? and when i play S:CE, can
i keep the .44 ?)

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
In article <7gkp95$csb$1...@trex.antw.online.be>,


Respectively:

No, since maneuvering with the weapon commits you to striking with that
weapon (as your initial strike of the round.

You are forced to use the absent .44, resulting in no strike.

You can dodge a canine horde, if you aren't already commited to another
strike.

S:CE will resolve before the canine horde attack, so you would keep the .44

--

Messages.Author: Vince Johnson
Messages.Body:
Halcyan 2 <halc...@aol.com> wrote in message
news:19990503173155...@ng-cm1.aol.com...


LSJ started to cover this in that last bit of the reply. only for your
first strike that round. 2nd and possible 3rd strikes may use any other
weapon. But you MUST use the gun during the first strike of that round and
as a result can not play a dodge to stop a canine horde to use the guns
later. Use of the gun is irrelevant, you must use it for the first strike
in that round.

Vince

Hey, I have a more basic question....if I use a dodge as an additional
strike, but the opposing vamp only has its regular strike (let's say
regular hand damage) and no add'l strikes, does the dodge have any effect?
In other words, can I use additional strikes to dodge original strikes?

Messages.Author: Vince Johnson
Messages.Body:
Kristyl Meth <dapa...@riderlaw.com> wrote in message
news:01be966a$5bbd8780$81a5...@dapatrin.riderlaw.com...


Nope, because each sub round of combat strikes has a damage dealing phase
where the effect has gone off already. You can't go back and undo something
that has already happened. You can however dodge and cancel your opponent's
non-strike(becuase he didn't have an additional strike) or dodge his
additional strike if he achieved one .

Vince

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
lao...@my-dejanews.com wrote:
> just to rekindle the old "1st strike vs dodge debate":
> LSJ cited the "dodge negates the opponents strike" even thought the 1st strike
> had already been resolved. what is the difference between these 2 scenarios?

Dodge cancels the opposing minion's (paired) strike. As such, it is
useful to say that strikes resolve in the following order:

1) Combat Ends
2) Dodge
3) Any other strike done at First Strike
4) Any other strike

Even though that may not be strictly correct.
Even if the "First Strike" resolved first, Dodge would still cancel the
effect - just like Sudden Reversal "cancels" the effect of the
already-resolved Master Card that it is being played in response to.

> dodge does not specify *which* strike it negates,

Yes it does: "it protects the dodging minion and his possessions from
the effects of *the* opposing *strike*." [6.4.5] (emphasis added).

Since strikes resolve in pairs, it is clear which of the opposing
minion's strike is "the" strike being cancelled.

A strike announced in an additional strike phase (announced after the
Dodge has already been resolved) would obviously not be affected.

A dodge announced in an addional strike phase (announced after all effects
of the initial pair of strikes have been fully resolved) would not undo
any of the initial pair of strikes' effects.
